label: hv-morph-segmentation
topic: Segmentation and somite statements: clock-and-wavefront (segment length = wavefront speed x clock period) and zebrafish somite numbers
summary:
Harvested 10 statements on vertebrate segmentation, formalized each, and validated three against numbers fetched in this session; one Lean file passed check.sh on its second run. Sources were PubMed abstracts and the ZFIN staging table, not full texts, so the exact numeric values inside the papers (23.5 min period, hes6 percent change, snake somite count) were NOT opened and are listed in could_not_find.

Registry status: grep for somite / wavefront / "segmentation clock" across lean, tracks/lean and tracks/research found no law for clock-and-wavefront. The only hits are incidental mentions in lean/genotype/dev-certificate.json, the turing-ddi proposal and requirement files, tracks/research/agents/bm-open-hardware-repro.json and tracks/research/doi-resolution.json (I did not open those files to see the context). So all ten statements are new to the registry.

Validation (ZFIN staging table, 28.5 C stage onsets: 1 somite at 10.33 h, 5 at 11.66 h, 10 at 14 h, 14 at 16 h, 20 at 19 h, 26 at 22 h):
- V1, constant clock period (one somite per 30 min throughout): FAIL for the first interval (4 somites in 1.33 h = 3.0 per hour, i.e. a 20 min period), PASS after that (2.14, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0 per hour). A constant-period law holds only from about somite 5-10 onward.
- V2, Lewis 2003 delayed-autoinhibition model, predicted period close to 30 min: PASS against the trunk rate of 2.0 somites per hour (30 min per somite) in the same table. Caveat: the paper itself compared to 30 min, so this is only an independent re-check of the observed value, not a blind test.
- V3, N = D / T for the counted window: from 11.66 h to 22 h (10.34 h) at T = 0.5 h predicts 20.7 somites; the table gives 26 - 5 = 21. PASS (within 2 percent). Stage boundaries are ranges, so precision is about +/- 1 somite.

Qualitative checks from abstracts only (direction, no numbers opened): slowed-clock zebrafish mutant has fewer segments (Schroter & Oates 2010) and Delta-Notch disruption gives longer period and correspondingly longer segments (Herrgen 2010): both agree in sign with S = v*T. Soroldoni 2014 is a stated FAILURE of the naive law: the oscillation period alone does not equal the segmentation period (Doppler contribution from tissue shortening).

Lean: D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/hv-morph-segmentation/ClockWavefront.lean, six theorems (segment length and number scaling with period, monotonicity, N = D/T, axis length), standard axioms only. First check run failed with an environment fault ("failed to read file ... CentroidHom.olean", the file exists; probably a concurrent reader); the second run, with the file unchanged, printed ALL CHECKED. These theorems are arithmetic consequences of the model, not evidence that the model is true.

Holdout: one harvested paper (Gomez 2008) compares four species including one from the held-out clade; I used only its snake/zebrafish/mouse statement and no data on the held-out clade. Any future test built on that paper must drop that species.

findings.claim: S1 Clock-and-wavefront core law: segment length S = v * T (v = wavefront speed relative to tissue, T = clock period). Assumptions: v and T constant over one cycle; one boundary per cycle. Registry: absent. Falsifier: per-embryo time-lapse measurements of v, T and S in zebrafish (Herrgen 2010 / Schroter 2008 supplementary tables); fail if S/(v*T) differs from 1 beyond measurement error.
findings.source: Cooke & Zeeman 1976, J Theor Biol, doi:10.1016/S0022-5193(76)80131-2 (NOT opened; statement of the model taken from the Schroter & Oates 2010 abstract, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2010.05.071)
findings.confidence: medium: model form is textbook, primary 1976 paper not opened
findings.evidence_quote: The Clock and Wavefront model for somitogenesis proposes

findings.claim: S2 Total segment number N = D / T, where D is the total duration of presomitic mesoderm growth and T the clock period. Assumption: one segment per cycle, T constant. Registry: absent. Falsifier: ZFIN staging table; fail if somite count over a window differs from window/T by more than 1-2 somites. Validated here (V3): predicted 20.7, table 21, PASS.
findings.value: N = D/T; 10.34 h / 0.5 h = 20.7 vs 21 observed
findings.confidence: high for the statement; validation precision about +/-1 somite
findings.evidence_quote: determined by the period of an oscillator or clock operating in the PSM

findings.claim: S3 Slowing the clock reduces segment number: T' > T with D and axis growth unchanged implies N' < N (N' = N * T/T'). Registry: absent. Falsifier: somite counts in the zebrafish hes6 period mutant versus wild type from the paper's figures; fail if the fractional drop in N does not match the fractional rise in T.
findings.value: direction confirmed; magnitude not in abstract
findings.confidence: high for direction, numbers not opened
findings.evidence_quote: This reduces segment number as predicted

findings.claim: S4 Longer period gives proportionally longer segments: disrupting Delta-Notch coupling raises the somitogenesis period, and segment length and gene-expression wavelength rise correspondingly (S'/S = T'/T at fixed v). Registry: absent. Falsifier: the multiple-embryo time-lapse period and segment-length tables of this paper; fail if the S ratio and T ratio differ beyond their error bars.
findings.value: direction confirmed; percent values not in abstract
findings.confidence: high for direction, numbers not opened
findings.evidence_quote: Embryonic segment length and the spatial wavelength of oscillating gene expression also increase correspondingly

findings.claim: S5 Zebrafish trunk somites form at a constant rate of 2 per hour (period 30 min) at standard temperature. Assumption: 28.5 C. Registry: absent. Falsifier: ZFIN staging table stage onsets. Validated (V1): intervals from 11.66 h to 22 h give 2.14, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0 somites per hour: PASS; but the first interval (10.33 to 11.66 h) gives 3.0 per hour: FAIL for a constant period over the whole series.
findings.source: https://zfin.org/zf_info/zfbook/stages/ (staging table after Kimmel et al. 1995, doi:10.1002/aja.1002030302; the 1995 paper itself not opened)
findings.value: 1 somite at 10.33 h, 5 at 11.66 h, 10 at 14 h, 14 at 16 h, 20 at 19 h, 26 at 22 h
findings.confidence: high; table opened, stage onsets are the lower bound of each range

findings.claim: S6 The cell-autonomous clock period is set by delays in a self-repressing gene loop; the delayed-autoinhibition model of her1/her7 predicts a period close to 30 min. Formal form (from the paper body, not opened): T approx 2*(T_delay + 1/b + 1/c), with b, c the protein and mRNA decay rates. Registry: absent. Falsifier: measured transcription/translation delays and half-lives for her1/her7 versus the observed 30 min period. Validated (V2) against ZFIN trunk rate 2.0 per hour = 30 min: PASS (not a blind test: the paper targeted 30 min).
findings.value: predicted period close to 30 min; observed 30 min per somite
findings.confidence: high for the abstract claim; the explicit formula is from memory of the paper body and was not opened
findings.evidence_quote: The predicted period is close to the observed period (30 min)

findings.claim: S7 FAILURE of the naive law: the period of segmentation is not equal to the period of the genetic oscillations; tissue shortening adds a Doppler term. Formal: 1/T_segmentation = 1/T_posterior_clock + (Doppler contribution from shortening) + (changing-wavelength contribution); S1 and S2 hold only if the tissue between clock and wavefront has constant length. Registry: absent. Falsifier: real-time reporter movies from this paper; fail if anterior and posterior oscillation counts are equal over the same time window.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1253089 (PubMed abstract, PMID 25013078; open full text PMC7611034 not read)
findings.value: qualitative; numeric period difference not in abstract
findings.evidence_quote: their time scale is not sufficient to explain the temporal period of segmentation

findings.claim: S8 Across species, segment number is set by clock rate relative to developmental rate: N proportional to (developmental duration) / T, and somite size falls as N rises. In snake embryos the clock runs much faster relative to development, giving many more, smaller somites. Registry: absent. Falsifier: the paper's per-species table of clock period, generation time and somite number (use snake, zebrafish, mouse only; the fourth species is in the held-out clade and must be dropped); fail if N does not rank with duration/T.
findings.value: qualitative; species numbers not in abstract
findings.confidence: high for the statement; numbers not opened
findings.evidence_quote: leading to a greatly increased number of smaller-sized somites

findings.claim: S9 Segmentation ends when the presomitic mesoderm, after first growing, shrinks to zero: D is the time at which PSM length L(t) reaches 0, with dL/dt = (axis elongation rate) - S/T. Assumption: mass balance of PSM tissue. Registry: absent. Falsifier: PSM length versus somite number curves in the same paper; fail if somites continue to form after PSM length reaches zero or stop while PSM remains.
findings.confidence: high for the statement; the differential form is my formalization
findings.evidence_quote: gradually shrinks until it is exhausted, terminating somite formation

findings.claim: S10 The collective period of coupled oscillators differs from the single-cell period and depends on coupling strength and coupling delay. Formal (delayed coupling theory, formula from the paper body, not opened): Omega = omega_A - epsilon * sin(Omega * tau), T = 2*pi/Omega. Registry: absent. Falsifier: periods of Delta-Notch mutants and inhibitor-treated zebrafish embryos (Herrgen 2010 tables); fail if the period does not shift when coupling is reduced. Notch is needed only for synchrony, not for boundary formation (Ozbudak & Lewis 2008).
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.2976/1.3027088 (PubMed abstract, PMID 19492022); supporting: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.0040015 (PubMed abstract, PMID 18248098)
findings.value: qualitative; explicit equation not in abstract
findings.confidence: high for the dependence; the explicit equation is from memory and unverified
findings.evidence_quote: the segmentation clock's collective period depends on delayed coupling

findings.claim: Registry check: no clock-and-wavefront, somite-number or segmentation-clock law exists in lean, tracks/lean or tracks/research; only incidental keyword hits in five files.
findings.confidence: medium: hit files were listed, not opened, so I did not confirm what each says about somites

findings.claim: Lean file ClockWavefront.lean: six theorems on the arithmetic of S = v*T and N = D/T check with standard axioms only (second run; first run hit an environment read fault on a Mathlib olean).
findings.confidence: high; I saw only the last lines of the output, with the axiom lists truncated by the script's summary line

key_claims: The registry has no clock-and-wavefront or somite-number law; all ten harvested statements are new.
ZFIN staging table: trunk somites form at 2.0 per hour (30 min period) from about somite 5 to 26, but the first four form at 3.0 per hour, so a constant-period law FAILS for the earliest somites.
N = D/T predicts 20.7 somites between 11.66 h and 22 h; the table gives 21 (PASS).
Soroldoni 2014 shows the naive law is incomplete: segmentation period is not the oscillator period because of a Doppler effect from tissue shortening.
ClockWavefront.lean passed check.sh (ALL CHECKED) on the second run; the first run failed on an environment file-read fault, not on the proofs.

recommendations: Add a clock-and-wavefront proposal to the registry with S = v*T and N = D/T as named-hypothesis theorems (ClockWavefront.lean is a starting point), and record S7 (Doppler effect) as a known limit of the law rather than hiding it.
Record V1 as a scoped result: constant 30 min period passes for somites 5-26 and fails for somites 1-5 in the ZFIN table.
For a quantitative test of S3/S4, open the Schroter & Oates 2010 and Herrgen 2010 full texts and compare the fractional period change with the fractional change in segment number and length.
Any cross-species test from Gomez 2008 must exclude the species from the held-out clade; use snake, zebrafish and mouse only.

lay_summary: A growing fish embryo cuts its back into a row of blocks called somites, which later become the backbone and muscles.
The leading idea is that a ticking clock inside the cells and a slowly moving line work together: each tick, one block is cut, so block length equals how far the line moved during one tick.
We checked this against a public zebrafish table: for most of the body one block forms every 30 minutes, just as predicted, and counting ticks gave 21 blocks where the table shows 21.

But the very first few blocks form faster, about one every 20 minutes, so the simple 'steady clock' rule fails there, and another study shows the rule also needs a correction because the tissue shrinks.
We also wrote the rule's arithmetic in a proof checker, which confirmed that a slower clock must give fewer, longer blocks.

glossary.somite: One of the repeated blocks of tissue along an embryo's back that later form backbone and muscle.
glossary.segmentation: Cutting the body axis into repeated blocks.
glossary.presomitic mesoderm (PSM): The strip of uncut tissue at the tail end from which new somites are made.
glossary.segmentation clock: Genes that switch on and off in a regular rhythm inside PSM cells.
glossary.clock period (T): The time for one full tick of the clock.
glossary.wavefront: A moving position in the tissue where cells become ready to form a boundary.
glossary.wavefront speed (v): How fast that position moves through the tissue.
glossary.clock-and-wavefront model: The idea that each clock tick places one boundary where the wavefront is, so segment length = speed x period.
glossary.oscillator: Anything that repeats a cycle, like a pendulum or a gene switching on and off.
glossary.Delta-Notch coupling: A signalling system by which neighbouring cells keep their clocks in step.
glossary.autoinhibition: A gene whose product switches the gene itself off.
glossary.transcriptional delay: The time needed to make a gene's message molecule.
glossary.Doppler effect: A change in observed rhythm when the source and observer move toward each other, as with a passing siren.
glossary.mutant: An animal with a changed gene.
glossary.period mutant: A mutant whose clock ticks slower or faster than normal.
glossary.hypothesis (in Lean): An assumption written out by name so the proof says exactly what it relies on.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A computer proof checker and its library of mathematics.
glossary.axiom: A basic starting assumption of the proof system; the three listed are the standard ones.
glossary.sorry / sorryAx: A placeholder for a missing proof; none are used here.
glossary.falsify: To show a statement is wrong with data.
glossary.stage onset: The time at which an embryo enters a named developmental stage.
glossary.registry: The project's list of formal laws already written down.
